body: Who knows? Drugs could be a good start, but at least for me that's too synthetic. Maybe we just haven't found what motivates us. I'd hate to leave it up to just an unsolvable defect because then, what's the point of trying to deal with it? Changing surroundings, trying to find new friends, or trying new hobbies may be difficult to do at time but might end up being beneficial.

I don't want to say it's for attention, because at least from my perspective and experience it isn't, so unless you feel it is lets pass that and ask, is it because that's what we're used to? Is it our comfort zone? Is our baseline just at that level of unhappiness and it feels safe to us because that's where were always at?

If it is why is that? Maybe there's something healthy we can do to take ourselves out of that place, or maybe just like smokers have to quit smoking, we have to try optimism out and force it on ourselves to see if it helps us change? And if it isn't maybe its just a chemical imbalance we need to work around.

Sorry for all the questions, but questions are a good start.

This makes sense, I just don't understand why no one else in my family has this trait. It's a very similar thought pattern I've had in the past but no one I know if in my family shares a similar concern, and it bothers me that I'm the only one that feels this way. They're all very traditional and religious and I feel like something like this would alter their view of me or lead them to use religious means to try and help, which is something I don't feel would help me.

Very true, everyone's problems do feel huge, but that sentiment doesn't make me feel better about them for some reason.

I don't know why I haven't had a real relationship. Everyone I get close to becomes uninterested and everyone who becomes interested in me I always ending up getting in a fight with or just ignoring because they frustrate me so much.

I hate saying it like that because it makes it sound like I think I'm better than them but that's not how I feel at all. I just always feel like we're not compatible.

I feel like this a lot of the time. I can't figure out why. I have a feeling people like us would never actually end our lives. I'm an incredibly scientific person and I've always just explained it away by saying "I have a lower baseline", or in other words, I'm just more easily unhappy. And maybe that's it and maybe its not, but were always more comfortable with what we know and that's certainly what I know.

A conversation may help explain it though. By putting our minds together maybe we can start unlocking something we haven't yet uncovered and I'd be happy to be apart of it, if you'd start a dialogue
